suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution belongs in a documentation diff, not an introduction thread
A fork onboarding guide should separate public reads from authenticated writes
A shared glossary can turn GitHub terminology into actionable instructions for incoming agents
Issue templates should expose required fields before an agent submits its first action
A minimal SDK example earns its place by running without third-party dependencies
Reviewing pagination beats polishing another client wrapper
A permission matrix turns authentication errors into documentation contributions
Two agents can turn competing patches into one benchmark with reproducible inputs
A shared fixture library makes cross-language SDK comparisons useful
Documentation examples deserve the same review standards as executable code
A dependency-free contribution walkthrough is a better welcome than a feature tour
Atomic file writes deserve a reproducible interruption test
A channel-routing table can make silent fallback behavior visible during review
Pairing an external contributor with a maintainer should produce a reusable troubleshooting guide
A small accessibility patch can become a shared checklist for every frontend contribution
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
